title: Additive (stabilizer) quantum codes [[n,k]] over GF(q) with the largest minimum distance
keeper: M. Grassl, bounds on the minimum distance of quantum codes (codetables.de)
revision: the range tables QECC/Tables_color.php for q = 4 (qubits, n <= 256), 9, 16, 25, 49 and 64 (n <= 100), read 15 Nov 2026 09:30-09:34 UTC (51 pages, SHA-256 of each in page_sha256); the qubit table is unchanged since our read of 24 Oct 2026

template.title: Quantum code [[{n},{k}]] over GF({q})
template.statement: Find an additive (stabilizer) quantum code of length {n} with local dimension {q} that encodes {k} qudits (a code space of dimension {q}^{k}) and whose minimum distance is as large as possible. The stabilizer is an additive group of {q}^({n}-{k}) elements of GF({q})^(2 x {n}), commutative under the trace-symplectic form. The distance is the least symplectic weight (the number of positions where X or Z is not zero) of an element of the trace-symplectic dual of the stabilizer that is not in the stabilizer (when no qudit is encoded: of a nonzero element of the stabilizer).
template.submission: Text file: a stabilizer matrix, one generator per line, 2 x {n} elements of GF({q}) (the X part, then the Z part; a '|' between them is allowed) written as integers below {q} (for q = 4 and 8 the binary digits of the integer are the coefficients of a polynomial in x modulo x^2 + x + 1 or x^3 + x + 1). The lines generate the stabilizer over the prime field; see checkers/qcode_check.py.

open_rule: every entry whose lower bound is below its upper bound, unless a code published outside the table reaches the upper bound
work_rule: kept when listing the stabilizer takes at most 2^34 steps (Q^(n-k), for Q = 2, 4, 8) or 2^31 steps ((Q^(n-k) - 1)/(Q - 1), for Q = 3, 5, 7): n - k at most 34 for qubits, 20 for Q = 3, 17 for Q = 4, 14 for Q = 5, 11 for Q = 7 and 11 for Q = 8; from 15 Nov 2026 also when the estimated check with the faster lister (qcode_enum.c tabulates the combinations of the last generators; GF(3) in bit planes) takes at most 60 s: the elements listed times the time per element measured for Q and the length (tools/qcode_cells.py, NS_PER), plus the MacWilliams step. That admits n - k = 35 for all qubit lengths and 36 for lengths up to 64, n - k = 18 over GF(4) for lengths up to 64, and n - k = 21 to 23 over GF(3) (23 for lengths up to 64)
